task: Auditory/cochlear transduction layer: cochlear tonotopy (Greenwood frequency-position map), basilar-membrane traveling-wave place mechanism + active cochlear-amplifier compressive nonlinearity, and a decorrelated ear-canal-resonance vs. threshold-of-hearing-minimum check.
confidence_tier: in-vivo-anchored (Greenwood 1990 human formula verified against independent cadaveric/imaging length measurements; Ruggero 1997 / Sellick 1982 direct in-vivo basilar-membrane mechanics; Keefe 2024 direct acoustic ear-canal measurement) -- amplifier GAIN MAGNITUDE explicitly held estimate-laden/regime-dependent, not a single certified number (see symmetric QC).

greenwood_1990.cite: Greenwood DD (1990). A cochlear frequency-position function for several species--29 years later. J Acoust Soc Am 87(6):2592-605.
greenwood_1990.verified_via: NCBI eutils efetch, abstract fetched live this session
greenwood_1990.note: Abstract is conceptual/methodological; does not itself print the A,a,k table.

stakhovskaya_2007.cite: Stakhovskaya O, Sridhar D, Bonham BH, Leake PA (2007). Frequency map for the human cochlear spiral ganglion: implications for cochlear implants. J Assoc Res Otolaryngol 8(2):220-33.
stakhovskaya_2007.verified_via: Open-access full-text PMC HTML fetched live this session; formula constants and length data extracted directly from the article text
stakhovskaya_2007.numbers: Quotes Greenwood 1990 verbatim: human A=165.4, a=2.1 (x=proportion of total BM length), k=0.88, giving 20-20,677 Hz. Independently measured (n=9 cadaveric cochleae, dissection, NOT derived from Greenwood's formula) organ-of-Corti length: mean 33.13mm (SD 2.11, range 30.5-36.87mm). Quotes two further independent studies: Sato et al 1991 (n=18: 32.3+/-1.8mm female, 37.1+/-1.6mm male) and Ketten 1998/Skinner 2002 (n=33: 33.4mm).

dorman_2007.cite: Dorman MF et al (2007). An electric frequency-to-place map for a cochlear implant patient with hearing in the nonimplanted ear. J Assoc Res Otolaryngol 8(2):234-40.
dorman_2007.verified_via: PubMed abstract fetched live this session
dorman_2007.numbers: Living-patient psychophysical (acoustic/electric) pitch-match test: Greenwood's acoustic map does NOT directly transfer to electrical spiral-ganglion stimulation -- pitch matches ~0.5-1 octave lower than predicted at 3-20mm insertion depth, saturating ~420Hz beyond 20mm. Concordant with Boex et al 2006.

ruggero_1997.cite: Ruggero MA, Rich NC, Recio A, Narayan SS, Robles L (1997). Basilar-membrane responses to tones at the base of the chinchilla cochlea. J Acoust Soc Am 101(4):2151-63.
ruggero_1997.verified_via: PubMed abstract fetched live this session
ruggero_1997.numbers: Direct in-vivo laser-velocimetry, chinchilla base (CF 9-10kHz). Linear gain 66-76dB re stapes (<10-20dB SPL); compressive I/O slope 'as low as 0.2 dB/dB' (40-80dB SPL); 'death abolishes all nonlinearities' and reduces CF sensitivity by 60-81dB.

sellick_1982.cite: Sellick PM, Patuzzi R, Johnstone BM (1982). Measurement of basilar membrane motion in the guinea pig using the Mossbauer technique. J Acoust Soc Am 72(1):131-41.
sellick_1982.verified_via: PubMed abstract fetched live this session
sellick_1982.numbers: Independent (different lab/species/decade/technique) confirmation: BM saturating nonlinearity in vivo, 'eliminated as CAP threshold became less sensitive and was absent post mortem.'

robles_ruggero_2001.cite: Robles L, Ruggero MA (2001). Mechanics of the mammalian cochlea. Physiol Rev 81(3):1305-52.
robles_ruggero_2001.verified_via: PubMed abstract fetched live this session
robles_ruggero_2001.numbers: Review corroboration + explicit regime caveat: 'At the apex of the cochlea, nonlinearities appear to be less prominent than at the base.'

oxenham_bacon_2003.cite: Oxenham AJ, Bacon SP (2003). Cochlear compression: perceptual measures and implications for normal and impaired hearing. Ear Hear 24(5):352-66.
oxenham_bacon_2003.verified_via: PubMed abstract fetched live this session
oxenham_bacon_2003.numbers: Qualitative cross-domain (physiological->psychophysical) corroboration: total OHC loss -> BM becomes linear -> accounts for poorer thresholds, loudness recruitment, reduced frequency selectivity.

part1_greenwood_falsifier.pre_registered_threshold: Greenwood's stated human constants (A=165.4,a=2.1,k=0.88) must reproduce Stakhovskaya 2007's own stated calibration numbers (20Hz, 20677Hz) within 2% relative error; AND Greenwood's assumed 35mm reference length must fall within 1 SD of the grand mean of 3 independent measured-length studies.

forced_adversary_fixed_mm_vs_proportiona.verdict: The naive fixed-mm simplification mis-predicts frequency by up to ~0.48 octaves across Stakhovskaya's own measured 30.5-36.87mm individual-length range; the proportional Greenwood formula has zero error by construction. Adversary forced and shown to measurably fail.

geometric_check.two_computational_paths: closed-form d(lnF)/dx vs. central finite difference
geometric_check.interpretation: Greenwood's function is near-pure-exponential (stiffness-gradient WKB regime) over the base/mid cochlea and inflates sharply only in the apical ~10-15%, exactly where the '-k' floor term is expected to matter physically (helicotrema/apex mass-dominated regime) -- a geometric derivation, not a bare curve-fit description.

part2_compression_falsifier.pre_registered_threshold: Living/dead BM-mechanical gain-loss-at-CF (Ruggero 1997: 60-81dB) must have non-empty numeric overlap with the independent OHC-ablation threshold-shift range (this repo's graph: 40-60dB); a pure gain-scaling adversary (ratio_dead/ratio_alive in [0.8,1.2]) must be checked against the cited compression-ratio numbers.
part2_compression_falsifier.overlap_honest_characterization: boundary-touching (0dB-wide overlap) -- real but narrow, not a comfortable match; two genuinely different measurement domains (mechanical BM velocity vs. behavioral/neural threshold).
part2_compression_falsifier.cross_domain_qualitative_leg: Oxenham & Bacon 2003 (PMID 14534407): OHC-loss linearization explicitly linked in review literature to loudness recruitment -- qualitative only, not quantitatively equated.

part3_ear_canal_falsifier.pre_registered_threshold: Quarter-wavelength resonance computed from an independent acoustic ear-canal-length measurement (Keefe 2024: 22.6+/-6.5mm, n=40) must fall inside [3,4]kHz.
part3_ear_canal_falsifier.honest_note: The CENTRAL estimate is robustly inside [3,4]kHz under both temperature assumptions; the +/-1SD POPULATION range is wider and its upper tail (canal shorter than average) extends past 5kHz -- real, disclosed inter-individual variability, not a uniformly tight match for every individual.
part3_ear_canal_falsifier.threshold_of_hearing_minimum_magnitude: NOT independently re-extracted from a live primary source (Suzuki & Takeshima 2004 full text paywalled) -- only the LOCATION (~3-4kHz) is cross-checked, carried from the task brief's own prior + this repo's pre-existing graph note (~2-5kHz).
part3_ear_canal_falsifier.contributory_not_sole_cause: Middle-ear transfer shape and intrinsic cochlear sensitivity also shape the threshold curve; ear-canal resonance is one genuine, independently-computable contributor to the minimum's LOCATION, not claimed as the sole cause.

overall_verdict.PASS_falsifier_2_amplifier_gain_overlap: true but boundary-touching/fragile, disclosed as such
overall_verdict.note: All 3 primary falsifiers pass on real, live-verified, non-tautological anchors. This is NOT presented as a clean sweep to celebrate: falsifier 2's numeric overlap is narrow/boundary-touching (disclosed), falsifier 3's population-level variability extends past the narrow task band at its tails (disclosed), and several structurally important pieces (exact ISO226 table, apex-region compression, electrical-vs-acoustic map transfer, amplifier gain's EXACT magnitude) are explicitly held OPEN per the task's own symmetric-QC brief.

symmetric_qc_open_items: The cochlear-amplifier GAIN MAGNITUDE is not a single certified number: direct BM-mechanical (60-81dB) and OHC-ablation threshold-shift (40-60dB) methods agree in order of magnitude and touch at a single boundary point (60dB), but are not claimed to coincide exactly -- two different measurement domains.
Compression calibration (Ruggero 1997) is basal/high-CF-specific (9-10kHz); Robles & Ruggero 2001's own review states apical nonlinearities are less prominent -- NOT extrapolated to all places/CFs.

Psychophysical (loudness recruitment) and physiological (BM mechanical) measures of compression loss are qualitatively concordant only (Oxenham & Bacon 2003) -- no quantitative dB/dB equivalence is claimed.

Greenwood's acoustic (organ-of-Corti) map does not directly transfer to electrical (spiral-ganglion) cochlear-implant stimulation without a measurable (~0.5-1 octave) correction (Dorman 2007/Boex 2006) -- a genuine, disclosed domain-of-validity boundary.
ISO226/Suzuki-Takeshima 2004's exact numeric threshold-of-hearing table was not independently extracted live (paywalled) -- only the minimum's LOCATION, not its magnitude, is cross-checked.
The stiffness-gradient e-folding length is a geometric INTERPRETATION of the verified Greenwood formula, not independently checked against a separate mechanical-stiffness paper.
Ear-canal resonance is a contributory, not sole, cause of the threshold-minimum location; the quarter-wavelength model idealizes the tympanic membrane as a rigid closed end.
